Ibrahim Khan: Hi everyone, Ibrahim here — first day. Trying to finish the dev bootstrap across my M1 Mac and a Linux VM. Running into two quick blockers:

1) asdf installed but when I run `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` it fails with `gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found` even after brew installing gpg.
2) the dotfiles bootstrap created copies of files instead of symlinks on my Linux VM (I expected symlinks).

Commands I ran:
```
brew install asdf direnv gpg
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
~/dotfiles/bootstrap.sh
asdf plugin-add nodejs
asdf install nodejs 18.16.0
```

Maya (DevEx): welcome Ibrahim! :tada: For the GPG issue with nodejs plugin try running the plugin's import script which fetches Node release keys: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. If that errors, explicitly pull the keyserver: `gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.openpgp.org --recv-keys 4ED778F539E3634C779C87C6D7062848A1AB005C`. Make sure the gpg binary in your PATH is the Homebrew one (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gpg` on arm mac).

Connor (Infra): about symlinks on the VM — check if the bootstrap detected `USE_COPY=1`. Some CI images set that to avoid broken symlinks. Run `env | grep USE_COPY` and re-run bootstrap after unsetting it. Also check that your VM filesystem supports symlinks (e.g., mounted with `-o user` can restrict).

Ibrahim Khan: I ran the import script but it still said `no valid OpenPGP data found`. `which gpg` shows `/opt/homebrew/bin/gpg`. Tried the keyserver receive and it timed out.

Maya (DevEx): keyservers can be flaky. Try using the plugin helper with explicit curl fallback: `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/master/README.md | grep -A2 "Node.js release signature"` — but safer: `brew reinstall gnupg` then `gpg --refresh-keys`. If your company proxy blocks hkps, try `gpg --keyserver hkp://pool.sks-keyservers.net --recv-keys <KEY>` as a fallback.

Connor (Infra): for the VM symlink problem — run `mount` and check options. If `/home` is on a CIFS/SMB mount or vbox shared folder, symlinks are often disabled. Move the dotfiles to a native ext4 path and re-run bootstrap: `mv ~/dotfiles /home/ibrahim/dotfiles && cd ~/dotfiles && ./bootstrap.sh`. The script creates `.dotfiles_backup_` by default; check there for copied originals.

Ibrahim Khan: moving repo to native ext4 and re-running made symlinks; thanks. For GPG I swapped the keyserver and `gpg --recv-keys` succeeded. Running the import script now finishes and node install started. One last small thing: my fish shell doesn't honor `export VAR=val` in .envrc — any lightweight approach to keep fish as my interactive shell?

Maya (DevEx): fish is fine, but many `.envrc` files expect POSIX. Two quick approaches: 1) temporarily run `bash` for direnv evaluation by adding a tiny wrapper: `.direnvrc` with `use bash` or 2) add a fish shim in `~/.config/fish/config.fish`: `if test -f $PWD/.envrc; bash -lc "source $PWD/.envrc && env" | while read -l line; set -xg (string split "=" $line)[1] (string replace -r '.*=' '' $line); end; end`. If that looks hairy, we recommend switching to zsh for day-to-day.

Dotfiles Bot: Canonical onboarding docs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles (see docs/mac-arm.md and docs/vm-notes.md). If you find a missing fallback, open an issue and tag @dev-ex.

Ibrahim Khan: All green now — node installed, symlinks fixed, and I added a small note to the dotfiles repo about the VM mount caveat. Thanks for the help! :rocket:
